# Harsh Critique

Harsh Critique is the golden-orange Pegasus stallion who goes from Daring Do convention cosplayer to outspoken critic of her books. He has a dark purple mane, bright green eyes and a distinctive explorer's pith helmet.

[![Harsh Critique (center), Friendship is Magic show artwork on Commentary Is Magic's Tarnished Reputation card](https://ponyhead.com/img/cards/nd139.jpg)](https://cardhuntershq.com/card/29671586/tarnished-reputation)

- **Name and continuity:** His appearances belong to the G4 television continuity, but his personal name comes from the community-produced New Dawn card expansion, not the show. Card #139, Tarnished Reputation, explicitly attributes its puppy-kicking quotation to Harsh Critique. The [Pegasus character index](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_ponies/Pegasus_ponies) identifies both appearances, and the [New Dawn printing page](https://databyte.fimfetch.net/ccg) identifies Commentary Is Magic as the set's designer.
- **Speaking status:** He speaks in Daring Doubt, credited generically as Pony 1 and voiced by Brian Drummond, according to the [episode cast listing](https://pro.imdb.com/title/tt10084482/). No separate speaking credit for his earlier appearance was established.

## Important moments

- **Daring Do cosplayer** — [Stranger Than Fan Fiction (S6E13)](https://transcripts.foreverdreaming.org/viewtopic.php?t=74156). He is identified as a convention booth attendant dressed as the adventurer, establishing his earlier connection to Daring Do fandom. Timestamp unavailable; the transcript does not identify him individually.
- **Confronting the author** — [Daring Doubt (S9E21)](https://transcripts.foreverdreaming.org/viewtopic.php?t=74216). At A.K. Yearling's book signing, he challenges the revelation that Daring Do is real and cites the accusation that she kicks puppies, showing how a rival author's account has damaged her reputation. Timestamp unavailable.

The card image and naming attribution were verified directly. The character index and cast listing were available in indexed excerpts, but their full pages could not be opened. No independently verified standalone fan artwork, cutie mark, or further appearances were found.
